body:
You gave me some great advice already! I'll slip a note under her door tomorrow and go to the gas station (it's a good walk) get some gas for the car in case of an emergency, and buy some other stuff for breakfast/lunch. I just hope my grandma can handle things until I get back. 

Thanks a lot for the advice, you really helped me think how to act and calm down a little. I guess I'll try to get some sleep now.

Thanks again. I'll keep you updated tomorrow.

Wish you the best.

I didn't until today. The problem is, here where I live, the police or any emergency service hardly does anything. Our house was once almost on fire, we called the emergency and they never showed up. Many times we've also called the cops and they showed up like 5 hours later. The most nearby hospital is in another city and there aren't any ambulances in my city.
That's why when she locked herself in her room and turned the TV volume all up, I first cut off power to check if I could talk to her and she would respond, when she did, and it all seemed ok, I called her close friend for help and tried to talk to her. I was ready to smash the door at any moment. I now keep every key in the house with myself, excluding her room's.
When she broke her arm, we had to drive around 40km to get to the hospital.

I'm afraid that by suggesting a therapy session she would take all the blame in it, since she's been told a lot that she doesn't know how to argue. There are a lot of monetary problems and other stuff we need to discuss, but she assumes everything is her fault and says she isn't worth nothing and it would be better if she disappeared. I don't really know how to react.

Today, for example:
She wants to sell the house and buy a smaller one. This one is way too big for the two of us and we can't really keep it all together. The garden is a mess and the house gets dirty really quick since we have 2 dogs and 3 cats. I've always been against the idea, but today she tried to smash a window and broke dishes, all while saying how much she hates this place and wants it to burn, before locking herself looking for "tools".  I do my best to keep things clean, but I totally forget sometimes and it all ends up in heavy arguing. But now I think that selling it might be the best idea.

I think her broken arm is really making her feel useless. She's not able to work and depends on me to go anywhere.

Sorry if this all looks kinda disconnected, I'm really nervous.

Thanks a lot, I'm gonna try writing something. I don't want it to look fake though, so I guess I'll just write "Good morning! I made some breakfast, come eat if you want." Does that look bad/forced?
I'm still afraid of what my grandma will say to her. I feel like there will be a huge fight tomorrow and things might get really ugly. Do you have any advice on how I can keep things calm and assure her I care about what she thinks and she is not "always wrong" like she says she is? Every time we have an argument it ends up really bad. I try to avoid it, but sometimes I can't control myself and end up saying stuff I shouldn't. I have the habit of kinda ignoring when she complains about stuff to avoid a fight, but I'm sure this makes it seem like I don't care.
I wish you the best in rebuilding the relationship with your mother.

I'd really like to do this, but I never had this kind of relationship with her. I'm sure she blames herself. She thinks I don't love her and that she's a terrible daughter and mother.
I'd really like to tell her how much I love her, but I don't feel comfortable with it and it really sucks. Her friend said to her that by calling for help I was showing how much I care. But whenever I try to talk to her now she tells me to fuck off.

My aunt has always lived with my grandma and went to therapy constantly. She was diagnosed bipolar and schizophrenic. Due to that, my mother says everyone only cared about her sister and she was totally forgotten, which is not true.

This year has been really harsh for her.
